metaDescription: CPT 98977 explained: the RTM device supply code for musculoskeletal monitoring and its 16-day data rule. Documentation, limits, 2026 rate and mistakes.
summary: The monthly device-supply code for musculoskeletal monitoring such as exercise adherence and pain or range-of-motion tracking. It requires data on at least 16 days in a 30-day period.
time: At least 16 days of data in a 30-day period
performer: Device supplied and data collected; no staff time threshold
requirements: Setup already documented (98975) and an active RTM order
A data log showing the days with musculoskeletal data
pitfalls: Billing with fewer than 16 data days when a shorter-window code applies
Using it for physiologic vitals that belong under RPM
conflicts: The 2026 short-window musculoskeletal supply code 98985 covers 2 to 15 days; it is not reported together with this code for the same period.

faqs.question: Which practices commonly use CPT 98977?
faqs.answer: Orthopedics, physical therapy, PM&R and pain management practices, where recovery depends on work done at home between visits.

faqs.question: Can therapists bill RTM?
faqs.answer: Yes. Unlike RPM, therapists can bill RTM, but the service needs a therapy plan of care and the GP, GO or GN modifier. Incident-to staff rules differ for therapists, so confirm payer and state rules.
